Subject: Production 429s + latency spike (NovaHealth) - urgent

Hi Grace / Marissa,

Starting ~08:10 PDT we're seeing a sharp spike in 429 responses and high tail latency from Redwood's API for our production tenant (novahealth-prod). Error rate climbed from ~0.2% to ~11% and p95 latency moved from 1800ms to ~4200ms. Throughput dropped ~30% as clients started backing off. We saw a cluster of 429s across multiple endpoints (chat/generate and embeddings).

Attached is a short sample (sample-logs.log) with request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether there were any rate-limit changes or policy updates on your side? This is impacting several customer workflows; we need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:31:00 -07:00
Subject: INVEST: ratecap override hit - NovaHealth (prod)

Marcus / Karthik —

Observed pattern from NovaHealth traces: a significant number of requests are receiving 429s which correlate with policy evaluation events. Early look at policy logs shows a "rate_cap_override" rule evaluated as TRUE against novahealth-prod, with an effective burst_window=0 for the account (i.e., no burst allowed). That would explain immediate 429s under short bursts.

Important constraints: this override was rolled out in the last policy release (yesterday ~22:30 PDT) to apply stricter limits to a subset of tenants flagged as "sensitive". NovaHealth does not qualify for tighter limits — we need confirmation whether they were mis-tagged or whether the rule selector is too broad.

Attachments: policy-diff.patch (config change), logs.zip (policy-eval snippets).

Ask: Can you validate the policy evaluation chain and either (A) roll back the override for novahealth-prod, or (B) apply an emergency temporary quota bump for them while we correct the selector? Please escalate to Runbook if needed.

— Grace
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INVEST: ratecap override hit - NovaHealth (prod)

On it — quick summary from infra triage:

1) Root cause: a policy regression in commit 9c4f7a (deployed 2028-05-10 22:18 PDT). The new "global_ratecap_override" introduced a condition that matches orgs with the SSO group tag "sensitive". A downstream mapping job erroneously synchronized NovaHealth's SSO group to include that tag (human error during group flattening). As a result, the policy engine evaluated burst_window=0 for them.

2) Scope: impacts novahealth-prod only (we've validated traffic patterns and policy hits). Canary and dedicated pools unaffected.

3) Immediate actions I will take now:
  - Push a targeted rollback of the policy selector for novahealth-prod (will flip the selector to exclude their org id). Expected propagation: ~12–18 minutes; ETA 09:03 PDT.
  - While rollback propagates, I'm authorizing a temporary soft quota increase via admin API (+30% burst allowance) to reduce 429s for active sessions (applies instantly).
  - Opened INF-7821 and created a short runbook entry for emergency rollback.

I've applied the soft quota bump and started the rollback on canary; will promote to prod on successful canary checks (ETA above). Logs and diffs attached (policy-diff.patch, logs.zip).

— Marcus
(attachment: policy-diff.patch, logs.zip)

Subject: Exec brief: NovaHealth production impact — recommended customer remediation/credits

Karthik —

Situation: NovaHealth experienced elevated 429s and latency for ~40 mins due to a policy regression that incorrectly applied a rate-cap override (burst_window=0) to their org. Marcus has performed a targeted rollback and applied a temporary quota bump; canary looks good. We estimate full recovery across all sessions within 10–15 minutes.

Customer impact: upstream product workflows degraded for several of NovaHealth's care partners; they are asking for an explanation and a goodwill gesture.

Ask: please approve the following immediate customer remedies so we can communicate with the customer: 
  - A credit equivalent to 25% of last month's bill (one-time)
  - A joint post-mortem and one-hour remediation call with their SREs next Tuesday
  - Priority audit of SSO group sync mappings (internal) and a policy rollback guard for future releases

I've drafted customer messaging and an MAP (mutual-action-plan.docx). If approved I'll send the external comms and propose the remediation timeline.

— Marissa
VP, Customer Success
